function.mechanism: Forms protective colloids/interfacial films to stabilize emulsions, with modest viscosity and texture effects in aqueous foods.

adi.basis: EFSA ANS (2017) and FAF (2019) concluded a numerical ADI is not required (no safety concern at reported uses).

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern for the general population or infants below 16 weeks under assessed use/exposure scenarios; recommendation to control impurities/specifications.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (evaluation year 1989, Meeting 49).

concerns.summary: Occupational exposure case reports describe allergic rhinitis/contact urticaria to gum arabic; EFSA FEEDAP (2025) also noted dermal and respiratory sensitisation risk for users/handlers.
As a fermentable soluble fiber, higher doses can increase bloating/flatulence/GI rumbling, though reported tolerability remained generally good in healthy adults.
Subchronic rodent oral study found no adverse toxicological findings at the highest tested dose (NOAEL at 5% diet, ~3.1-3.3 g/kg bw/day).

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA (2017) re-evaluation: no genotoxicity concern and no consumer safety concern at reported use levels.
EFSA (2019) infant follow-up: no safety concern in infants below 16 weeks under assessed scenarios.
JECFA ADI not specified and longstanding authorization history in major jurisdictions.

adi_exceedance.notes: Exposure can be high on a body-weight basis in children, but EFSA/JECFA do not set a numerical ADI for E414; EFSA did not identify a safety concern at assessed exposures.

risk_assessment.rationale: The additive is broadly approved (EU/FDA/JECFA) with ADI not specified/not required and no major systemic toxicity signal at intended dietary uses, but limited caveats remain for occupational sensitisation and mild high-dose GI intolerance.
key_factors: US CFR GRAS framework and defined use conditions
